name: Offensive Lob
summary: An offensive lob is played out of a dinking rally, lifted over the opponents at the kitchen line and into the back of their court. Done well it wins the point outright because nobody can turn and run in time. Done badly it is the easiest overhead they will see all day, which is why it has to be rare and disguised.
whenToUse: Both opponents are leaning in, crowding the kitchen line and watching the ball low.
You are dinking cross-court, so the lob has the longest diagonal to travel.
There is wind or sun behind you that makes tracking it harder.
You have been dinking patiently long enough that nobody expects it.
howTo: Set up exactly as you would for a dink — same stance, same low contact.
Take the ball out in front and below the waist.
Lift with the legs and the shoulder, keeping the wrist quiet so the height stays repeatable.
Aim over the shoulder of the backhand side, deep toward the baseline.
Send it high enough that it cannot be reached, not just high enough to clear them.
Move up as it travels — if it comes back, it comes back short.
commonMistakes: Changing your stance before you hit it, which announces it a full second early.
Lobbing to the forehand side, where the overhead is comfortable.
Not enough height, which is simply a slow ball at head height in front of a net player.
Lobbing from a ball that was already below your knees, where the lift has nowhere to come from.
Trying it more than once or twice a game, at which point they just stop leaning in.

drills.name: Same swing, two shots
drills.description: Dink cross-court with a partner. Every fifth ball is a lob, but the setup has to look identical. Your partner calls it out loud the moment they read it — if they are calling it early, the disguise is not there.

drills.name: Over the backhand shoulder
drills.description: Place a cone or a bag on the backhand side of the opposite baseline area. Lob from a dink and score only the ones that land past it, over that shoulder.

mistake.label: Too low: it clears them by a foot and lands mid-court, which is an overhead they were already under.
